themes_detail.label: Underground Infrastructure Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Root/sewer/sidewalk condition complaints surged to 3 THIS WEEK versus a 0.1 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks—a 2,300% spike (z-score: 8.69)—suggesting a potential major subsurface failure or widespread deterioration in Fordham/University Heights' underground infrastructure.
evidence: 3 root/sewer/sidewalk complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (2,300% increase, z-score 8.69)
Sidewalk condition complaints also spiked to 6 THIS WEEK vs. 1.8 weekly average (243% increase, z-score 3.54)
Coupled with elevated obstruction complaints (5 in prior 2 weeks vs. 1.1 avg, 344% increase)
reporting_angles: File FOIL request with NYC Department of Environmental Protection and Department of Sanitation to identify specific blocks affected and whether emergency repairs are underway
Interview residents and local business owners about visible sidewalk damage, sinkholes, or water main breaks observed in the past 7–10 days
Examine whether community board's standing request for additional sanitation trucks and equipment is linked to capacity gaps in responding to subsurface emergencies

themes_detail.label: Street Vendor Enforcement Surge
themes_detail.summary: Vendor enforcement complaints jumped to 7 THIS WEEK against a 2.1 weekly baseline over the prior 8 weeks—a 229% spike (z-score: 3.58)—indicating either a new enforcement push or emerging illegal vending activity in the district.
evidence: 7 vendor enforcement complaints THIS WEEK vs. 2.1 weekly average (229% increase, z-score 3.58)
No prior reporting in local media or Reddit discussions, suggesting this is an emerging phenomenon
Spike is acute and narrowly recent, not a multi-week trend
reporting_angles: Contact NYC Department of Finance Street Vendor enforcement office to determine if there's a coordinated sweep in Fordham or University Heights this week
Interview street vendors in the district about recent tickets, seizures, or increased enforcement presence
Investigate whether complaints are concentrated in specific commercial corridors (e.g., near Grand Concourse, Jerome Ave, or near Fordham University campus)

themes_detail.label: Exterior Building Deterioration
themes_detail.summary: Outside building complaints spiked to 5 THIS WEEK versus 0.9 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks—a 471% increase (z-score: 6.88)—potentially signaling widespread exterior facade, fire escape, or structural defects affecting multiple properties.
evidence: 5 outside building complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.9 weekly average (471% increase, z-score 6.88)
281 DOB building permits filed in last 90 days, with 143 alterations and 8 demolitions—high construction activity may be triggering new code violations or facade failures
No corresponding decline in other housing-related complaints, suggesting this is additive stress
reporting_angles: Request Department of Buildings violation data for the past 14 days; cross-reference addresses with 311 complaints to map clusters of exterior violations
Conduct visual survey of residential buildings along major streets (Grand Concourse, Webster Ave, University Ave) to photograph loose bricks, deteriorated fire escapes, or bulging facades
Interview DOB and FDNY about whether recent weather events (heavy rain, wind, freeze-thaw cycles) may have accelerated building envelope degradation

themes_detail.label: Food Safety Cluster (3 weeks ago)
themes_detail.summary: Food poisoning complaints peaked at 4 approximately 3 weeks ago—a 967% spike versus a 0.4 weekly baseline (z-score: 5.21)—but signal is aging and no current outbreak confirmation exists; requires verification of whether cluster has resolved or ongoing.
evidence: 4 food poisoning complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 0.4 weekly average (967% increase, z-score 5.21)
No recent Reddit posts or local news coverage of an outbreak, making verification difficult
Spike is 3 weeks old; current status of those complaints unknown
reporting_angles: Contact NYC Department of Health and Mental Hygiene to obtain records of confirmed foodborne illness investigations and restaurant closures from 3 weeks ago through present
Interview affected residents (if identifiable via DOH records) about suspected sources and symptoms
Determine whether the spike was linked to a single venue or dispersed across multiple food service locations

themes_detail.label: Residential Disposal Mismanagement (3 weeks ago)
themes_detail.summary: Residential disposal complaints spiked to 5 approximately 3 weeks ago—a 400% increase versus 1.0 weekly baseline (z-score: 4.0)—potentially indicating a temporary sanitation collection failure or coordinated illegal dumping; current status unclear.
evidence: 5 residential disposal complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 1.0 weekly average (400% increase, z-score 4.0)
Community board has standing budget request for additional sanitation trucks, suggesting persistent resource constraints
Spike is aging; no recent corroborating complaints or media mentions
reporting_angles: File FOIL request with NYC Department of Sanitation for collection schedules, missed pickup reports, and equipment breakdowns from 3 weeks ago
Interview district sanitation managers about whether a specific collection route or facility experienced outages mid-month
Check current 311 complaint rate for disposal issues to confirm whether problem has resolved or become endemic
